newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITIMPEKS COMPLETES 60 MLN LITAS SHARE ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: LITIMPEKS COMPLETES 60 MLN LITAS SHARE ISSUE.

text.p: Lithuania's Litimpeks Bank said on Tuesday that it had completed its 60 million litas share distribution to Western, Scandinavian and Baltic investors.
"Shares of 36 million litas were bought by Scandinavian and Western investors, eight million by Estonians and the remaining part by local investors from Lithuania," the bank said in statement. "
The statement said Norwway's Skeie Group, Norwegian Oil Trading Company and Uber See Bank of Zurich were represented in distribution.
The share capital of Litimpeks now stands at 64 million litas.
The share issue may signal a new beginning for the troubled bank, which was closed by the central bank for six months in 1995 and 1996.
"Litimpeks is back," said Jonas Bobelis, vice-president of Litimpeks.

"That's (the share distribution) stage one and we're looking to continue forward and we're back in fighting shape," Bobelis said, adding that the bank wanted to rekindle relationships with customers it lost during its closure.
The closure of Litimpeks and Lithuanian Joint-Stock Innovation Bank in December 1995 sparked a nationwide banking crisis that weighed heavily on the sector during 1996.
Litimpeks was able to claw its way back to solvency but Innovation is in the process of being liquidated.
The bank's losses in 1996 were 6.37 million litas and 1.9 million litas in the first quarter of 1997.
